runs.content: YTD 2026 (all through Sep 11, compounded from Q1 x Q2 x Q3, computed directly from yfinance price history via etf_returns.py -- the ETFreplay-scraping pipeline was retired this run): IWD +22.4%, IWN +22.0%, IWM +17.9%, QQQ +16.6%, SPY +12.7%, IVE +11.8%, IWF +3.5%. Growth vs value spread: IWD +22.4% vs IWF +3.5% -> value leads by 1884 bps, essentially unchanged from 1880 bps on Sep 4. Notable: a broad pullback hit every ETF this week, but small caps far harder than large caps -- IWM's Q3 partial swung from -1.5% to -3.9% (YTD +20.8% -> +17.9%, the largest weekly move of any ETF) and IWN's from +1.6% to -0.7% (YTD +24.7% -> +22.0%). Large caps held up better: IWF Q3 -0.6% -> -1.5% (YTD +4.5% -> +3.5%), QQQ -2.4% -> -2.9% (YTD +17.3% -> +16.6%), IWD +6.3% -> +5.4% (YTD +23.3% -> +22.4%), IVE +4.3% -> +3.6% (YTD +12.5% -> +11.8%). Because growth and value fell by similar amounts, the spread barely moved, but the sharper small-cap value selloff knocked IWN out of first place -- IWD is now the top YTD performer for the first time in 2026. QQQ-IWF divergence widened to 1314 bps (from 1280 bps), the first widening in three weeks.

runs.content: YTD 2026 (all through Sep 4, independently compounded from Q1 x Q2 x Q3 -- matched ETFreplay's own annual/YTD readout to within rounding this run, no discrepancies found): IWN +24.7%, IWD +23.3%, IWM +20.8%, QQQ +17.3%, SPY +13.5%, IVE +12.5%, IWF +4.5%. Growth vs value spread: IWD +23.3% vs IWF +4.5% -> value leads by 1880 bps, down from 1980 bps on Aug 28 -- a third compression this quarter (after Aug 7 and Aug 28). Notable: growth kept firming through the first week of September -- IWF's Q3 partial improved from -1.1% to -0.6% (YTD +3.9% -> +4.5%) and QQQ's Q3 partial improved from -2.7% to -2.4% (YTD +16.9% -> +17.3%) -- while value gave back ground for the first time this quarter (IWD's first YTD decline of the year, +23.7% -> +23.3%; IVE +12.8% -> +12.5%). Small caps mixed: IWM ticked up (+20.6% -> +20.8%), IWN accelerated further (+23.9% -> +24.7%), widening its lead over IWD to 1.4pp. QQQ-IWF divergence eased slightly to 1280 bps (from 1300 bps). IWN remains top YTD performer.
